note: 'who say to Zion, Your God reigns!' (Isa 52:7). The message has an addressee and it is a place.

Two verses apart in one argument: Rom 10:13 quotes Joel on calling upon the name and Rom 10:15 quotes Isaiah on the feet that bring the message. Paul does not join them in a sentence -- he runs from one to the other by asking how anyone calls on him they have not heard of.
'who proclaim peace' (Isa 52:7); 'those who bring good news' (Rom 10:15).

'What God promised our fathers He has fulfilled for us, their children' (Acts 13:32-33). The promise is named and not quoted, so which promise is the graph's reading -- but Peter cites this one to the same audience at Acts 3:25, and it is the promise the fathers were given.
'As He has said: I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.' (Acts 13:34), quoting Isa 55:3 two verses after the glad tidings are declared.

Isaiah's messenger brings good tidings; Acts 13:32 declares glad tidings. The corpus uses the same word for both in this translation and Acts does not cite Isaiah here, so the tie is by vocabulary rather than by quotation -- and Rom 10:15, which does quote Isaiah, calls the same thing the gospel.
